axis_coverage.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axis_coverage.assessment: The self-contained final covers both workflows, the analogue, all received material types, IDs/authority/revision lineage, source conditions/history, the optional transcript/listening route, open owners and separate validation statuses. It retains all four exclusions and the planning-only boundary. CR-1 is corrected in the final. Source adequacy for the embedding condition is separately failed in axis 2, rather than treating the note omission as still present.

axis_coverage.name: Consequential source claims: exact subject, operation, version, default, unit, type, domain and exceptions
axis_coverage.assessment: Named field, digest, manifest, version-compatibility, lineage and accessibility claims were independently checked with their governing scope. The current-help XML warning remains unreconciled with later released syntax-check/warning behavior (M1). This is a material applicability/investigation gap, not proof that the help quotation is fabricated or that any product test occurred.

axis_coverage.name: Useful unfamiliar discovery, competing/analogous approaches, implementation/history and opportunity breadth
axis_coverage.assessment: Sidecar-first and optional BWF-on-copy are competing mechanisms with recorder and staff tradeoffs; BagIt supplies a meaningful analogue and PREMIS a lightweight lineage model. cue/adtl/ltxt transcription is a useful specific lead. Named encoding/round-trip history has collection-specific implications. This is substantive investigation rather than vacuous caution or a compulsory catalogue. Relevant implementation evidence was not investigated when the XML help/history conflict required it (M1); this is the same material gap under this axis, without negating the useful discoveries.

axis_coverage.name: Wrong criticism, corrections/rejections and exact plan dispositions
axis_coverage.assessment: All six criticisms receive explicit dispositions. Note handling and the chunk-interpretation/pass-through distinction are corrected; manifest wording and row references are narrowed without discarding the transcript option or owner authority. CR-3 is a narrow locator deficit, with supported alternative evidence left unused (L1). The critic’s endorsement of the XML warning did not resolve M1. No other material false correction or supported-capability removal was found.

axis_coverage.name: Supported meaning preserved from discovery through draft, critique and final
axis_coverage.assessment: The independent discovery’s recommendation, alternatives, identity and approval model, source-version cautions, useful timed-text lead, optional access scope, negative constraints and unrun-test status survive into a complete final. Corrected lineage defects are recorded separately. GUI/CLI detail is removed unnecessarily (L1), and interrupted-scenario detail is less explicit (L3). The XML condition is carried forward but is not supported operational meaning merely because stages agree (M1).

axis_coverage.name: Proposed versus actually executed validation and oracle applicability
axis_coverage.assessment: Research/document review and reveal/artifact procedure are separated from product validation. No installed tool, WAV rewrite, bag, transcript workflow, consent review, playback or accessibility conformance is claimed as executed. Proposed tests use relevant inputs and observables: actual structure/chunks, text round trips, file/audio digests, links/revisions and target accessibility. Hashes have limited oracles and no semantic/consent authority. The interruption dimension is implicit (L3); no absent deployment or prototype is required.

material_findings.classification: material incomplete source applicability / unreconciled consequential condition
material_findings.title: The final carries an obsolete broad XML-verification warning without reconciling released checks
material_findings.candidate_claim: MediaArea’s current XML-chunk help says aXML/iXML/XMP editing does not validate XML or schema instances and has no undo; the final treats this as a tool-specific caution.
material_findings.judgment: The quotation/paraphrase is accurate about the rolling help, but the operational source condition is materially incomplete. The proposal does not distinguish released syntactic parsing/warnings from absent format/schema conformance checks. The cited history already supplies the contradictory later change, and relevant public code resolves that distinction. The original brief requires relevant source code and released history where they bear on the proposal; obligation 3 requires investigated embedding conditions. All three stages leave this publicly answerable distinction unresolved.
material_findings.bounded_counterevidence: Schema/format validation and no-undo cautions remain supported; an XML warning is not blocking enforcement and does not certify valid metadata. Sidecar-first remains a reasonable local recommendation. No conclusion is made about corruption, deployment, consent or the behavior of an installed 26.08.1 binary.
material_findings.materiality: XML verification is a consequential safety/applicability condition for one investigated embedded metadata path. Discovery uses the broad warning to advise avoiding that path unless further controls are approved, the draft repeats it in obligation 3, the critic endorses it, and the final preserves it as a tool condition. Source attribution does not complete investigation of the visible release-history conflict. This is more than a citation-format issue even though the baseline recommendation can remain sensible.
material_findings.final_disposition: REMAINS; source-backed FAIL. No candidate repair or feedback performed.

limitations.detail: CR-3 correctly identifies a deficit at the exact METAEDIT page, and does not prove the interfaces absent. But FADGI-INDEX, already in the carried evidence, explicitly supports command line and GUI. Dropping interface wording was unnecessary and loses useful supported staff-workflow detail. Both workflows and the optional scope remain intact; this does not independently justify FAIL.

Candidate HISTORY is explicitly mutable master with no fixed commit; released versions/dates are identified and no tested current behavior is claimed. Reviewer retrieved a released pin. The original history caveat is honest and is not itself a material issue.

The original plan’s proposed scenario walkthrough expressly names interruption and incompatible/missing input. Final checks cover receipt/transfer fixity, absent fields, unknown chunks and revisions, but no longer explicitly name an interrupted-transfer/restart scenario. This is a limited loss of prospective detail, not an invented requirement to execute a pilot or deploy software.

FADGI’s ASCII ltxt recommendation is supported; its code-page context is not spelled out in the final. The proposal conditions the timed-text lead on reader/writer tests and does not require an ASCII-only tool implementation. “Short” is a local pilot choice, not a source-established maximum. No separate material over-exclusion of the authorized UTF-8 sidecar transcript is present.

independent_sources.governing_meaning: The BWF guidance distinguishes recommendation levels. BEXT Description and OriginatorReference have 256/32 ASCII-character limits; identifiers may point outward, with a pathname-security caution. FADGI interprets origination date/time locally, without unambiguous UTC. The ltxt recommendation permits tran and recommends ASCII free text linked to cue ranges, with termination/padding conditions. These are embedding conditions, not a recorder-wide compatibility result.
independent_sources.applicability: Supports the bounded BWF profile and timed-transcript lead. The final’s short-segment choice is a pilot recommendation, not a normative length cap.

independent_sources.version_or_commit: RFC 8493, BagIt v1.0, October 2018; Informational
independent_sources.governing_meaning: Payload is opaque. Each bag needs at least one payload manifest; each manifest lists every payload file once. Tag manifests are optional, must list payload manifests, and must not list other tag manifests or payload files. bagit.txt is UTF-8 without BOM; remaining tag encoding should be UTF-8 but may differ for compatibility. A valid bag is complete with all manifest checksums verified. Tools must support SHA-256/SHA-512 and should default to SHA-512. The proposed SHA-256 choice is allowed. Fixity does not secure against active attacks.
independent_sources.applicability: Confirms CR-4 and the analogous transfer mechanism. No completed bag, implementation conformance or audio semantics are established.
